needs.text: octopus has large brain-to-body ratio comparable to mammals
needs.context: Octopuses are incredibly intelligent creatures for several reasons. Firstly, their large brain-to-body ratio is comparable to that of some mammals. Secondly, they have the ability to learn and remember complex behaviors, such as opening jars and solving mazes. Thirdly, they have excellent problem-solving skills and can adapt to new environments quickly. Finally, they have the ability to camouflage themselves by changing the color and texture of their skin, which requires a high level of cognitive processing. All of these factors contribute to the exceptional intelligence of octopuses.

needs.text: asks whether to get tank mate for octopus or if octopus will eat companion
needs.context: Should I get my octopus a friend to play with in his tank or will he eat them?

needs.text: octopuses are solitary animals that do not benefit from tank mates
needs.context: Octopuses are solitary creatures and do not typically benefit from having tank mates. In fact, adding another octopus to your tank could lead to aggressive behavior, cannibalism, or other negative interactions. Octopuses are known to be opportunistic predators, and they will often consume any smaller animals or invertebrates in their vicinity, including other octopuses. Therefore, it's best to avoid introducing another octopus to your tank and focus on providing your octopus with a stimulating and enriching environment on its own.
